external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the supplier document portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: Supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.notes: The vendor's datasheet says the platform is secure by design, that it uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, that all access is fully authenticated and audited, and that the product is fully compliant.

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: A service in our cloud account that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where supplier compliance documents remain stored.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A landing bucket in our cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The supplier database in our cloud account where the supplier master service writes extracted records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork through the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it through the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decision

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The supplier document portal stores uploaded documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance documents and contact details

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: Conflicting claims about encryption in transit: System description says, "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." The runbook says, "the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is."

data_flows.name: load file
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the supplier data extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes extracted supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract

trust_boundaries.name: Supplier
trust_boundaries.description: The suppliers' environment, controlled by suppliers outside the system.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor platform
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment containing the SaaS portal and stored documents.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: Our cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier paperwork and records are confidential because they include insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The vendor platform stores compliance documents and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket data is confidential because it contains the nightly supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The landing bucket receives a supplier data extract containing supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database data is confidential because it contains supplier records derived from the extract.
assumptions.basis: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
